question:
An 68-year-old man arrives at an urgent care center with sudden-onset shortness of breath. He is alert
and interactive but unable to provide a detailed medical history, except for a smoking history of one
pack per day from age 15 to 60. He is unsure of his medications, as his daughter manages his pillbox,
but he denies using inhalers. Over the past week, he has experienced worsening dyspnea, both at rest
and during activity. He also has a chronic cough that has recently worsened, producing clear sputum
without changes in volume or purulence. Five days ago, his primary care physician prescribed
furosemide 40 mg daily, which has not alleviated his symptoms. On examination, his blood pressure is
111/70 mm Hg, heart rate is 89 beats per minute, and oxygen saturation is 92% on room air. Lung
auscultation reveals diminished air entry with bilateral crackles at the bases that clear with coughing,
along with expiratory wheezing. A cardiac exam identifies a 3/6 holosystolic murmur at the left lower
sternal border, which intensifies with inhalation. His internal jugular venous pressure (JVP) is 11 cm

H■O, rising to 16 cm with abdominal pressure and returning to baseline within 2–3 seconds. His lower
extremities show erythema and 1+ pitting edema to the mid-ankle, which the patient reports has been
stable for a month. Laboratory results include a serum creatinine level of 0.9 mg/dL (reference range:
0.8–1.3), hemoglobin concentration of 10.2 g/dL (13.5–17.5), and N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic
peptide (NT-proBNP) level of 1337 pg/mL (10–131). Which of the following interventions is most likely
to alleviate this patient’s dyspnea? Answer Choices: (A) Add spironolactone 50 mg daily, and continue
furosemide 40 mg daily (B) Initiate therapeutic anticoagulation with enoxaparin (C) Begin digoxin 0.125
mg daily (D) Increase the dose of furosemide to 80 mg daily (E) Begin prednisone 40 mg daily and
inhaled ipratropium (F) Start oral amoxicillin-clavulanate for 7 days (G) Start combination inhaled
fluticasone/salmeterol (H) Start supplemental oxygen at 2L/min via nasal cannula (I) Add lisinopril 10
mg daily (J) Begin oral metoprolol 25 mg twice daily
 A. Begin oral metoprolol 25 mg twice daily
B. Start supplemental oxygen at 2L/min via nasal cannula
C. Increase the dose of furosemide to 80 mg daily
D. Begin digoxin 0.125 mg daily
E. Add lisinopril 10 mg daily
F. Start oral amoxicillin-clavulanate for 7 days
G. Begin prednisone 40 mg daily and inhaled ipratropium
H. Start combination inhaled fluticasone/salmeterol
I. Initiate therapeutic anticoagulation with enoxaparin
J. Add spironolactone 50 mg daily, and continue furosemide 40 mg daily
